card.name: Words after poison and toxin subjects
card.fires_on: The word right after a poison, toxin or toxic-chemical subject, such as a verb, auxiliary or modifier leading to a harmful outcome. It also fires on the word poisoned itself in stories about poison.

modes.label: Verb after toxin subject
modes.description: A linking verb or modifier directly after a toxin-producing or toxic subject, leading to harm.
modes.example: Hypertoxin producing strains of C. difficile cause<< increased>> morbidity and mortality, as these infections

modes.label: Poisoned itself
modes.description: The word poisoned in a narrative about poisons.
modes.example: In the middle ages some poisons were reputed to have been administered by contact: and there are many stories of<< poisoned>> rings used for such a purpose.

modes.label: Toxic chemical settings
modes.description: A word in a sentence about exposure to toxic metals or chemicals.
modes.example: Workers can be exposed to cadmium in air from the smelting and refining of metals, or from the air in plants that<< make>> cadmium products such as batteries, coatings
